title: The Challenges Faced by Women in Leadership with Alice Eagly, PhD

sentences.en: 2020 is the 100th anniversary of women winning the right to vote in the United States, yet full equality for women in this country remains elusive.
sentences.zh: 2020年是美国女性获得投票权100周年，然而在这个国家，女性实现完全平等依然遥不可及。

sentences.en: Yes, U.S.
sentences.zh: 是的，美国。

sentences.en: Senator Kamala Harris is the Democratic nominee for vice president, which is certainly significant, yet she's only the second black woman ever to be elected to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯参议员是民主党的副总统候选人，这当然意义重大，但她只是美国历史上第二位当选的黑人女性。

sentences.en: Senate, which has only seen 57 female members since the dawn of our country.
sentences.zh: 参议院自建国以来总共只有57名女性成员。

sentences.en: Only one quarter of the Senate is female today, while the much larger House, with 435 members, is 23% female.
sentences.zh: 如今参议院中女性仅占四分之一，而规模大得多的众议院共有435名成员，其中女性占比为23%。

sentences.en: The number of women at the top of the business world is also scant.
sentences.zh: 商业界高层中的女性人数也寥寥无几。

sentences.en: We have just reached an all-time high of 37 women CEOs of the Fortune 500, but that means that almost 93% of those top companies are led by men.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚达到了《财富》500强企业中女性CEO人数的历史最高点——37位，但这也就意味着这些顶尖公司中近93%仍由男性领导。

sentences.en: Why has it taken so many years for women to make even these gains?
sentences.zh: 为什么女性花了这么多年才取得这些进展？

sentences.en: What are the particular challenges faced by women who strive to be leaders?
sentences.zh: 那些努力成为领导者的女性面临着哪些特殊的挑战？

sentences.en: How can psychology help us better understand the factors that hold women back or push them down or discourage them from aiming for the top?
sentences.zh: 心理学如何帮助我们更好地理解那些阻碍女性、打压女性或让她们对追求高位望而却步的因素？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that explores the connections between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Alice Eggly, a professor of psychology at Northwestern University,
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是西北大学心理学教授爱丽丝·埃格利博士，

sentences.en: who for many years has studied the psychology of gender, especially sex differences and similarities
sentences.zh: 多年来她一直研究性别心理学，特别是性别差异与相似性，

sentences.en: in leadership, pro-social behavior, aggression, partner preferences, and socio-political attitudes.
sentences.zh: 涉及领导力、亲社会行为、攻击性、伴侣偏好和社会政治态度等领域。

sentences.en: Dr. Eggly has written numerous articles, chapters, and books on these topics.
sentences.zh: 埃格利博士就这些主题撰写了大量的文章、章节和书籍。

sentences.en: Her most recent book, Through the Labyrinth, The Truth About How Women Become Leaders, challenges the common metaphor of the glass ceiling.
sentences.zh: 她最近的著作《穿越迷宫：女性如何成为领导者的真相》挑战了“玻璃天花板”这一常见的隐喻。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Eggly.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学谈话》，埃格利博士。

sentences.en: I'm pleased to be here, Kim.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，金。

sentences.en: This is not the first time a woman has been on the vice presidential ticket in this country, and women have run for president, although only once, as a major party candidate.
sentences.zh: 这并不是这个国家第一次有女性出现在副总统候选人名单上，女性也曾竞选过总统，尽管作为主要政党候选人只有一次。

sentences.en: Is there something different about what's happening now, and are the reactions from the media and the public different this time around?
sentences.zh: 现在发生的事情有什么不同吗？媒体和公众的反应与以往相比有何不同？

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: I think that it was entirely expected, even demanded, of a Democratic candidate, such as Joe Biden, because their support for the Democratic Party is stronger among women than men.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全是意料之中的，甚至是被要求的，因为像乔·拜登这样的民主党候选人，女性对民主党的支持率要高于男性。

sentences.en: So it really called for women being represented.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实需要女性代表。

sentences.en: And then it's a time when there's a good deal of protest and unrest over minority issues.
sentences.zh: 而且现在正值针对少数群体问题的抗议和动荡时期。

sentences.en: And so choosing a woman of color certainly made sense to represent that community,
sentences.zh: 因此，选择一位有色人种女性来代表该群体当然是有意义的，

sentences.en: which tends to lean Democratic, but to, you know, to call on their loyalty in this particular way.
sentences.zh: 该群体倾向于支持民主党，你知道，这也是为了以这种特殊方式呼吁她们的忠诚。

sentences.en: So I think it was entirely expected and generally very well received.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是完全意料之中的，而且总体上非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's been interesting that there has not been a whole lot of backlash, I think.
sentences.zh: 是的，有趣的是，我认为并没有出现太多的强烈反对。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: I mean, what are the characteristics that make her less of a target?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是什么特质让她受到的攻击较少？

sentences.en: She is quite qualified in the sense that she had a number of political roles in California,
sentences.zh: 她非常有资格，因为她在加州担任过多个政治职务，

sentences.en: and she is a senator, and so she has very good qualifications that would be normal in a male candidate.
sentences.zh: 而且她是一位参议员，所以她具备男性候选人通常所拥有的非常好的资历。

sentences.en: So she's qualified in that sense.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，她是合格的。

sentences.en: She's also quite gifted as a speaker and a debater, as was displayed earlier in the hearings in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 她也是一位非常有天赋的演讲者和辩论者，正如之前在参议院听证会上所展示的那样。

sentences.en: So I think she struck the public as, you know, somebody who had the toughness to be a good campaigner.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为她给公众留下的印象是，你知道，一个有韧性去成为一名优秀竞选者的人。

sentences.en: So what particular challenges do women politicians face first as candidates and then once they're elected?
sentences.zh: 那么，女性政治家在作为候选人时，以及一旦当选后，会面临哪些特殊的挑战？

sentences.en: Well, there are serious challenges that are embedded in the culture in a sense,
sentences.zh: 嗯，从某种意义上说，这些严重的挑战是根植于文化之中的，

sentences.en: in terms of the way we think about leaders and the way we think about women and men.
sentences.zh: 就我们对领导者的看法，以及我们对男女的看法而言。

sentences.en: So this is well established in studies on stereotyping, done by psychologists and political scientists in this case.
sentences.zh: 这一点在心理学家和政治学家所做的刻板印象研究中已经得到了充分证实。

sentences.en: So we know that people think women are the nicer, kinder, more compassionate sex, more sympathetic to others,
sentences.zh: 我们知道，人们认为女性是更友善、更温柔、更富有同情心、更体贴他人的性别，

sentences.en: better social skills, and that men are the tougher, more agentic, we call it, more assertive, more aggressive sex.
sentences.zh: 拥有更好的社交技巧；而男性则是更强硬、更具能动性（我们称之为“agentic”）、更果断、更具攻击性的性别。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We know about that.
sentences.zh: 我们了解这一点。

sentences.en: But then people think about leaders as more agentic than communal.
sentences.zh: 但人们又认为领导者应该更具能动性，而非共融性。

sentences.en: So they think about, you know, they have to take charge.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为，你知道，他们必须掌控全局。

sentences.en: They have to be tough, tell people what to do often.
sentences.zh: 他们必须强硬，经常告诉别人该做什么。

sentences.en: So that image is widely shared in the culture and is much more similar to men than women.
sentences.zh: 这种形象在文化中被广泛认同，而且与男性的形象更为相似，而非女性。

sentences.en: And so that puts women at something of a disadvantage.
sentences.zh: 这让女性处于某种劣势。

sentences.en: And it sort of goes like that.
sentences.zh: 情况大概就是这样。

sentences.en: Well, she's, you know, she's very nice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，她人很好。

sentences.en: But then the but is, you know, I don't know if she's tough enough to handle that kind of situation.
sentences.zh: 但随之而来的“但是”是，你知道，我不知道她是否足够强硬来处理那种情况。

sentences.en: Could she really hold up in a big debate?
sentences.zh: 她真的能在大型辩论中坚持住吗？

sentences.en: You know, could she get people to do things?
sentences.zh: 你知道，她能让人们听从指挥吗？

sentences.en: Would she have the respect and authority?
sentences.zh: 她会有威望和权威吗？

sentences.en: And so that lingers in the culture.
sentences.zh: 所以这种想法在文化中挥之不去。

sentences.en: And so women have to overcome, in a sense, these anxieties people have.
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种意义上说，女性必须克服人们心中的这些焦虑。

sentences.en: It's not about being a good person or a competent person.
sentences.zh: 这与是否是一个好人或有能力的人无关。

sentences.en: It's about being a tough enough person to really take on that kind of role that demands a lot of competition and assertion.
sentences.zh: 这关乎是否足够强硬，能够承担那种需要大量竞争和主张的角色。

sentences.en: And yet, if you're too tough as a woman, then that cuts against you as well.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你作为女性表现得太强硬，那也会对你不利。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's the agency paradox.
sentences.zh: 这就是“能动性悖论”。

sentences.en: So if you're very assertive, like, so you say, well, okay, I'll be just like a man.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你非常果断，比如你说，好吧，我会表现得像个男人一样。

sentences.en: Wrong.
sentences.zh: 错了。

sentences.en: That doesn't really work for women.
sentences.zh: 这对女性来说并不奏效。

sentences.en: Unless, you know, it could take on qualities of being assertive to some extent, but not to go to the extremes is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 除非，你知道，在某种程度上可以表现出果断的特质，但走向极端是危险的。

sentences.en: But add to it the qualities of warmth and kindness and empathy.
sentences.zh: 但要加上温暖、善良和同理心的特质。

sentences.en: So display both.
sentences.zh: 所以要两者兼顾。

sentences.en: That tends to be something that works for women who are leaders or wish to be leaders.
sentences.zh: 这往往对那些已经是领导者或希望成为领导者的女性有效。

sentences.en: And you can see that in Kamala Harris right away.
sentences.zh: 你可以立刻在卡玛拉·哈里斯身上看到这一点。

sentences.en: She speaks in a clear, pleasantly assertive way.
sentences.zh: 她说话清晰，语气令人愉悦且果断。

sentences.en: She smiles a lot, too.
sentences.zh: 她也经常微笑。

sentences.en: And has a lot of feminine expressiveness in her gestures and voice.
sentences.zh: 而且在手势和声音中有很多女性化的表现力。

sentences.en: Not too much, but it's definitely there.
sentences.zh: 不过分，但绝对存在。

sentences.en: And so I think she has that blend that, in fact, works very well for women in leadership roles.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为她拥有那种融合的特质，事实上，这对于担任领导角色的女性非常有效。

sentences.en: You recently published a study that looked at a large body of nationally representative public opinion polling and found that women are now perceived as being just as competent as men,
sentences.zh: 你最近发表了一项研究，考察了大量具有全国代表性的民意调查，发现女性现在被认为与男性一样有能力，

sentences.en: as well as more communal.
sentences.zh: 而且更具共融性。

sentences.en: But they're seen as less ambitious.
sentences.zh: 但她们被认为野心较小。

sentences.en: How have these views changed over the past decades?
sentences.zh: 这些观点在过去几十年里发生了怎样的变化？

sentences.en: Is this good news for women leaders today?
sentences.zh: 这对今天的女性领导者来说是好消息吗？

sentences.en: It's mixed news.
sentences.zh: 这是喜忧参半的消息。

sentences.en: So this study was based on representative public opinion poll data where people were asked about men and women.
sentences.zh: 这项研究基于具有代表性的民意调查数据，人们被问及关于男性和女性的问题。

sentences.en: And the data go back to 1946 and then through 2018.
sentences.zh: 数据可以追溯到1946年，一直到2018年。

sentences.en: So it's quite a nice series.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常好的系列数据。

sentences.en: And so the way the pollsters do this is they ask a very direct question.
sentences.zh: 民调机构的做法是提出一个非常直接的问题。

sentences.en: They say, like, intelligence, more true of women, more true of men, or equally true.
sentences.zh: 他们会问，比如智力，是女性更符合，男性更符合，还是同样符合。

sentences.en: And so we do see a lot of change in that women's competence relative to men has risen.
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到了很大的变化，女性相对于男性的能力有所提升。

sentences.en: So most Americans now say equal.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数美国人现在认为两者平等。

sentences.en: But those who don't say equal are more likely to say women than men.
sentences.zh: 但那些不认为平等的人，更有可能说是女性而非男性。

sentences.en: So their competence leans slightly in the female direction.
sentences.zh: 所以她们的能力略微偏向女性方向。

sentences.en: So that would be like being intelligent.
sentences.zh: 这就像是聪明才智一样。

sentences.en: The other change is rather unexpected to many observers, I think, or social scientists in particular, that the communion of women versus men has increased.
sentences.zh: 另一个变化对许多观察家，特别是社会科学家来说是相当出乎意料的，那就是女性相对于男性的共融性增加了。

sentences.en: So now it's overwhelmingly true if you say something like sympathetic, more true of women than men.
sentences.zh: 所以现在如果你说像“富有同情心”这样的词，绝大多数人会认为女性比男性更符合。

sentences.en: It's women.
sentences.zh: 是女性。

sentences.en: So that has changed over time to be more extreme.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，这一点变得更加极端。

sentences.en: And agency doesn't change.
sentences.zh: 而能动性并没有改变。

sentences.en: So 1946, people saw men as more aggressive and assertive than women.
sentences.zh: 所以1946年，人们认为男性比女性更具攻击性和果断性。

sentences.en: And they still do.
sentences.zh: 现在依然如此。

sentences.en: And there's just no significant change in that trend.
sentences.zh: 这一趋势没有任何显著变化。

sentences.en: So for women not to be troubled by these stereotypes, it's the agency that has to change as well as the competence.
sentences.zh: 因此，女性要摆脱这些刻板印象，不仅能力需要改变，能动性也需要改变。

sentences.en: People have to see women as tough enough.
sentences.zh: 人们必须认为女性足够强硬。

sentences.en: And that still goes in the male direction.
sentences.zh: 而这一点仍然偏向男性方向。

sentences.en: The competence is very helpful.
sentences.zh: 能力是非常有帮助的。

sentences.en: You know, if anything, women are somewhat more competent than men because competence is something people expect of leaders.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果说有什么不同的话，女性在某种程度上比男性更有能力，因为能力是人们对领导者的期望。

sentences.en: And the communion is probably not particularly effective in terms of being seen as even more communal than women in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 而共融性在被视为比过去更具共融性方面，可能并不是特别有效。

sentences.en: Well, what do you think is different in other countries?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为其他国家有什么不同？

sentences.en: I mean, women are still underrepresented in leadership in America, but other industrialized countries have been led by women.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，女性在美国的领导层中仍然代表性不足，但其他工业化国家已经由女性领导过。

sentences.en: You know, you can think of Germany or England or even New Zealand today.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以想到今天的德国、英国甚至新西兰。

sentences.en: What's different there?
sentences.zh: 那里有什么不同？

sentences.en: The political scientists explain that there's women have better chances at a parliamentary system than a presidential system.
sentences.zh: 政治学家解释说，在议会制下，女性比在总统制下有更好的机会。

sentences.en: So in a parliamentary system, you know, the executive and the legislative branches are combined because the prime minister is the head of the party that wins.
sentences.zh: 在议会制中，你知道，行政和立法部门是结合在一起的，因为总理是获胜政党的领袖。

sentences.en: It has the majority.
sentences.zh: 它拥有多数席位。

sentences.en: And so women can make their way up through good service and popularity in their own districts up the hierarchy in the party, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以女性可以通过在自己选区的良好服务和受欢迎程度，在政党等级制度中晋升，你知道，

sentences.en: like Margaret Thatcher and a couple of others.
sentences.zh: 就像玛格丽特·撒切尔和其他几位一样。

sentences.en: And you can make it to the top of your party.
sentences.zh: 你可以进入政党高层。

sentences.en: And then, by the way, you get to be prime minister if your party is elected.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你的政党当选，你就能成为总理。

sentences.en: They don't elect a person directly.
sentences.zh: 他们不是直接选举一个人。

sentences.en: They elect a party.
sentences.zh: 他们选举一个政党。

sentences.en: But we don't have that.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有那种制度。

sentences.en: We have the separate executive.
sentences.zh: 我们有独立的行政部门。

sentences.en: And so the focus is all on this one role.
sentences.zh: 所以焦点全在这个单一角色上。

sentences.en: And, you know, being a woman or a man, you're voting for the person.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，无论是女性还是男性，你投票选的是那个人。

sentences.en: And I think that brings out the difficulties that women have, even in the UK, because they're never voted for as a person when they get to be prime minister.
sentences.zh: 我认为这凸显了女性面临的困难，即使在英国也是如此，因为当她们成为总理时，她们从来不是作为个人被投票选出的。

sentences.en: And then the other thing, in some countries, and it happened a little bit here, as an attempt, you know, there's a passing on through family, very elite family ties.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，在一些国家，这里也发生过一点尝试，你知道，通过家族传承，非常精英的家族纽带。

sentences.en: And so Indira Gandhi was Nehru's daughter.
sentences.zh: 比如英迪拉·甘地是尼赫鲁的女儿。

sentences.en: And, you know, and so some countries have that passing on.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，所以有些国家有这种传承。

sentences.en: And if there's not a male to pass it on to, it might get passed on to a wife in some cases or, you know, to a child.
sentences.zh: 如果没有男性可以传承，在某些情况下可能会传给妻子，或者，你知道，传给孩子。

sentences.en: Of course, we had a hint of that with the Clintons, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在克林顿夫妇身上看到了这种迹象，不是吗？

sentences.en: AlmoSt.
sentences.zh: 差不多。

sentences.en: But it didn't go when all was said and done.
sentences.zh: 但最终并没有实现。

sentences.en: But it's not a tradition in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但这在美国并不是一种传统。

sentences.en: to do that.
sentences.zh: 去那样做。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There was the two bushes, so it looked like we did it, though.
sentences.zh: 有两位布什总统，所以看起来我们确实做到了。

sentences.en: But anyway, it's a stronger tradition in some other countries where it's happened at an earlier point, you know, as when Indira Gandhi was prime minister of India.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，这在其他一些国家是一种更强的传统，在更早的时候就发生过，你知道，比如英迪拉·甘地担任印度总理时。

sentences.en: So there are differences in the governmental system.
sentences.zh: 所以政府体制存在差异。

sentences.en: There may be differences in attitudes, too, but it's particularly the structure of the political system, I think.
sentences.zh: 态度可能也存在差异，但我认为主要是政治体制的结构问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, we would tend to see some of those cultures as being even more sexist than the United States.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们倾向于认为其中一些文化比美国更具性别歧视。

sentences.en: But yet, like Pakistan and India and other countries have had.
sentences.zh: 但像巴基斯坦、印度和其他国家却有过女性领导人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Benazir Bhutto, yeah, same situation.
sentences.zh: 贝娜齐尔·布托，是的，同样的情况。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And have had women.
sentences.zh: 而且有过女性。

sentences.en: And they tend to have been closely aligned in the narrow elites that were in the, you know, often by blood.
sentences.zh: 她们往往与狭隘的精英阶层紧密结盟，你知道，通常是血缘关系。

sentences.en: And, you know, so in your book, Through the Labyrinth, you challenge the notion of the glass ceiling,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，所以在你的书《穿越迷宫》中，你挑战了“玻璃天花板”的概念，

sentences.en: that solid but somewhat invisible barrier that most of us think women face when it comes to reaching the highest echelons of leadership.
sentences.zh: 即我们大多数人认为女性在达到最高领导层时所面临的那种坚固但有些隐形的障碍。

sentences.en: Why do you think that metaphor is not apt and that a labyrinth is closer to the challenges that women face?
sentences.zh: 为什么你认为那个隐喻不恰当，而“迷宫”更接近女性面临的挑战？

sentences.en: Well, there's a couple of reasons, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，至少有几个原因。

sentences.en: One is excess.
sentences.zh: 一个是过度。

sentences.en: It suggests a very solid barrier.
sentences.zh: 这暗示着存在一道非常坚固的屏障。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's like prejudices aren't like that.
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为偏见是那样的。

sentences.en: They are more fungible and malleable.
sentences.zh: 它们更具可替代性和可塑性。

sentences.en: And it isn't that we've never had women as, for instance, CEOs in the Fortune 500.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我们从未有过女性担任《财富》500强企业的首席执行官。

sentences.en: So there are some and have been others.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有一些，也曾经有过其他人。

sentences.en: But the other reason, it suggests that the barrier is right near the top, right?
sentences.zh: 但另一个原因在于，它暗示这道屏障就在顶层附近，对吧？

sentences.en: So you move up through your career and, oh, my God, you can't be CEO because there's this barrier at the top, next to the top.
sentences.zh: 所以当你职业生涯不断晋升时，天哪，你却无法成为首席执行官，因为在顶层或接近顶层的地方有这道屏障。

sentences.en: But that's not how it works in terms of careers in management or other areas that involve leadership.
sentences.zh: 但就管理或其他涉及领导力的领域而言，职业发展并非如此运作。

sentences.en: The challenges are all along the way.
sentences.zh: 挑战始终贯穿于整个过程。

sentences.en: It's in day one.
sentences.zh: 从第一天就开始了。

sentences.en: You go to work as a manager just coming in with your MBA.
sentences.zh: 你刚拿到工商管理硕士学位，以经理身份入职。

sentences.en: The challenges you have as a woman are there.
sentences.zh: 作为女性，你所面临的挑战就在那里。

sentences.en: And they're there every day.
sentences.zh: 而且每天都在。

sentences.en: And as you rise, there are different challenges.
sentences.zh: 随着你的晋升，会有不同的挑战。

sentences.en: You know, it goes on and on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这没完没了。

sentences.en: So it isn't as if you're exactly the same as men and then near the top there's a glass ceiling.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说你和男性完全一样，只是在接近顶层时才有一道玻璃天花板。

sentences.en: It's really a completely wrong metaphor.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个完全错误的隐喻。

sentences.en: You know, it has some truth to it, perhaps, but it doesn't adequately represent the nature of the challenges, which are all along the way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它或许有一定道理，但并不能充分体现挑战的本质，因为挑战始终贯穿全程。

sentences.en: And so that's why we propose labyrinth, that the man has a relatively straight road.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们提出“迷宫”这个概念，因为男性走的是一条相对平坦的道路。

sentences.en: You know, maybe he has some bumps along the way or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许他沿途会遇到一些颠簸之类的。

sentences.en: But the woman has to go through this labyrinth.
sentences.zh: 但女性必须穿过这个迷宫。

sentences.en: So she has to be smarter, right?
sentences.zh: 所以她必须更聪明，对吧？

sentences.en: And she has to figure out how to overcome these challenges that she might face as a woman.
sentences.zh: 她必须想办法克服作为女性可能面临的这些挑战。

sentences.en: She might take a wrong turn, but, you know, it's possible to turn around and go on, you know, if you're really persistent.
sentences.zh: 她可能会走错路，但你知道，如果你足够坚持，还是可以回头继续前进的。

sentences.en: But you've got to expect you might get confused at some time and, you know, take a wrong turn.
sentences.zh: 但你必须预料到自己有时可能会感到困惑，并走错路。

sentences.en: So it more represents the true complexity of women's careers in leadership than a glass ceiling does.
sentences.zh: 因此，相比“玻璃天花板”，它更能代表女性领导者职业生涯的真实复杂性。

sentences.en: You published a meta-analysis in 2011 that examined the extent to which stereotypes of leaders are culturally masculine.
sentences.zh: 您在2011年发表了一项荟萃分析，考察了领导者刻板印象在多大程度上具有文化上的男性化特征。

sentences.en: Can you talk about those findings and whether these stereotypes have changed in the intervening years?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这些发现，以及这些刻板印象在随后的几年里是否发生了变化吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We did publish a meta-analysis.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发表了一项荟萃分析。

sentences.en: It involved actually three underlying types of studies that had looked at the leader stereotype.
sentences.zh: 它实际上涉及了三种研究领导者刻板印象的基础研究类型。

sentences.en: The most famous paradigm was started by Virgin Shine, and it's called the Think Manager, Think Male paradigm.
sentences.zh: 最著名的范式是由维吉尼亚·沙因（Virginia Schein）开创的，被称为“想到经理，想到男性”范式。

sentences.en: It started first in 1973.
sentences.zh: 它始于1973年。

sentences.en: And in that study, there are three groups of participants.
sentences.zh: 在那项研究中，有三组参与者。

sentences.en: One rates women, one rates men, and one rates managers or leaders.
sentences.zh: 一组评价女性，一组评价男性，另一组评价经理或领导者。

sentences.en: And they do it on a long list of traits.
sentences.zh: 他们根据一长串特质进行评价。

sentences.en: And then they correlate these ratings, the men group to the leader group and the woman group to the leader group.
sentences.zh: 然后他们将这些评分进行相关性分析，即男性组与领导者组的相关性，以及女性组与领导者组的相关性。

sentences.en: And they find the male leader correlations are much higher than the woman leader correlations, which is just what we said before.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，男性与领导者的相关性远高于女性与领导者的相关性，这正是我们之前所说的。

sentences.en: People think that leaders are, you know, masculine and assertive.
sentences.zh: 人们认为领导者是那种男性化且果断的人。

sentences.en: And so men are more like leaders than women are.
sentences.zh: 所以男性比女性更像领导者。

sentences.en: And so that's why it got called the Think Manager, Think Male paradigm.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它被称为“想到经理，想到男性”范式。

sentences.en: And so it started in 1973, so we could look at it over many years.
sentences.zh: 它始于1973年，所以我们可以观察它多年来的变化。

sentences.en: And we did find some shift.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发现了一些转变。

sentences.en: And that was the woman leader's relationship.
sentences.zh: 那就是女性领导者的相关性。

sentences.en: There was some gain in thinking that leaders had more feminine characteristics, that is, in particular, more social skills.
sentences.zh: 人们在认为领导者具有更多女性特质，特别是更多社交技能方面，确实有所增加。

sentences.en: So the notion of leader had changed so that, yes, people continued to think that leaders need to be tough and assertive.
sentences.zh: 所以领导者的概念已经改变了，是的，人们仍然认为领导者需要强硬和果断。

sentences.en: But, by the way, they should be somewhat socially skilled.
sentences.zh: 但顺便说一句，他们也应该具备一定的社交技巧。

sentences.en: And so it was a hint of androgyny coming in.
sentences.zh: 所以这预示着一种双性化特质的出现。

sentences.en: But still, the masculine characteristics won out over the feminine, even in the most recent study.
sentences.zh: 但即便在最近的研究中，男性化特征仍然胜过女性化特征。

sentences.en: So it was a shift that would be welcoming to women, this growth of androgyny.
sentences.zh: 所以这种双性化特质的增长对女性来说是一种受欢迎的转变。

sentences.en: But it didn't go all the way to androgyny.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有完全演变成双性化。

sentences.en: It just was some addition of the social skills, sympathy, empathy kind of thing to what people expect for leaders.
sentences.zh: 它只是在人们对领导者的期望中，增加了一些社交技能、同情心和共情能力之类的东西。

sentences.en: You've also looked at differences in pro-social behaviors between men and women.
sentences.zh: 您还研究了男性和女性在亲社会行为方面的差异。

sentences.en: How are they different and how are they the same?
sentences.zh: 它们有何不同，又有何相同之处？

sentences.en: Pro-social behavior encompasses a lot of different kinds of behaviors.
sentences.zh: 亲社会行为涵盖了许多不同类型的行为。

sentences.en: And so we found that both sexes engage in pro-social behavior, a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 我们发现两性都会参与亲社会行为，而且参与度很高。

sentences.en: So they're similar in engaging in this class of behaviors.
sentences.zh: 所以在参与这类行为方面，他们是相似的。

sentences.en: But they tend to specialize, to some extent, in different aspects.
sentences.zh: 但他们在不同方面往往会有所侧重。

sentences.en: And one of the things we were interested in, in particular, was pro-social behavior, where the helper puts him or herself at some risk.
sentences.zh: 我们特别感兴趣的一点是那种让施助者自身承担一定风险的亲社会行为。

sentences.en: And that was interesting because there was a lot of differentiation.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为存在很大的差异。

sentences.en: So men are more likely to do physically dangerous acts to save other people's lives, such as saving somebody from drowning,
sentences.zh: 男性更有可能为了挽救他人的生命而做出身体上危险的行为，比如从溺水中救人，

sentences.en: running into a burning building and pulling out somebody, intervening in a crime setting where the criminal has a gun.
sentences.zh: 冲进燃烧的建筑物救人，或在罪犯持有武器的犯罪现场进行干预。

sentences.en: And so these are truly life-threatening.
sentences.zh: 这些确实是危及生命的。

sentences.en: And although women sometimes do these things, it's considerably less likely.
sentences.zh: 虽然女性有时也会做这些事，但可能性要小得多。

sentences.en: But another thing that has some danger is living kidney donation.
sentences.zh: 但另一件具有一定危险性的事情是活体肾脏捐献。

sentences.en: You know, giving your kidney, you're a perfectly healthy person, and this person's kidneys have given out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，捐献你的肾脏，你是一个完全健康的人，而对方的肾脏已经衰竭了。

sentences.en: And would you jump up and say, well, you can have mine?
sentences.zh: 你会挺身而出说，好吧，你可以用我的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's not an easy decision because it involves not actually a lot of risk, but it involves an operation and some real risk to your health and whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是一个容易的决定，因为它涉及的风险虽然不是特别大，但涉及手术以及对你健康的一些真实风险等等。

sentences.en: And we find women are more likely to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们发现女性更有可能这样做。

sentences.en: It's to give parts of their body.
sentences.zh: 也就是捐献身体器官。

sentences.en: It's often done in family.
sentences.zh: 这通常发生在家庭内部。

sentences.en: It's within families because the more you're genetically matched, you know, the safer it is for the person who receives it.
sentences.zh: 因为基因匹配度越高，对接受者来说就越安全。

sentences.en: But women are more likely to, and highly disproportionate for giving to a spouse, women are much more likely to give to a husband than husband is to a wife.
sentences.zh: 但女性更有可能这样做，尤其是对配偶的捐献，女性捐给丈夫的可能性远高于丈夫捐给妻子。

sentences.en: That's pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太令人惊叹了。

sentences.en: So there's a dangerous kind of helping behavior, but it's somewhat female-dominated.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种危险的助人行为，但它在某种程度上是由女性主导的。

sentences.en: So other kinds, you know, volunteer organizations, such as doctors and nurses who go into dangerous situations and that kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 还有其他类型的，你知道，志愿组织，比如医生和护士，他们会进入危险境地，诸如此类，

sentences.en: women are very well represented in those kinds of organizations, even though they're so brisk.
sentences.zh: 女性在这些组织中的代表性非常高，尽管这些工作节奏很快。

sentences.en: Of course, there's a higher proportion of women nurses.
sentences.zh: 当然，女性护士的比例更高。

sentences.en: Yeah, but both nurses and doctors and even psychologists are needed in those situations because they're traumatic.
sentences.zh: 是的，但在这些情况下，护士、医生甚至心理学家都是必需的，因为这些经历会造成创伤。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So another thing we looked at, it took quite a lot of time to gather all the available data,
sentences.zh: 所以我们研究的另一件事，花了相当多的时间来收集所有可用数据，

sentences.en: data was Holocaust rescuing by non-Jewish persons, which happened in the occupied countries of Europe.
sentences.zh: 数据是关于非犹太人对大屠杀幸存者的营救，这发生在被占领的欧洲国家。

sentences.en: And there were records.
sentences.zh: 而且有记录可查。

sentences.en: They're actually kept by Yad Vashem, which is an organization in Israel.
sentences.zh: 这些记录实际上由以色列的亚德瓦谢姆大屠杀纪念馆保存。

sentences.en: And they are held at the Holocaust Museum in Washington, from which we got the records, from which we could classify the people by nationality and sex.
sentences.zh: 它们保存在华盛顿的大屠杀纪念馆，我们从那里获得了记录，并据此按国籍和性别对这些人进行了分类。

sentences.en: And we found women slightly overrepresented.
sentences.zh: 我们发现女性的比例略高。

sentences.en: Often, you couldn't tell because it was a couple, you know.
sentences.zh: 通常你无法分辨，因为那往往是夫妻档，你知道的。

sentences.en: But then when there were individuals recognized for having rescued, there was a slight overrepresentation of women.
sentences.zh: 但当个人因营救行为受到表彰时，女性的比例确实略高。

sentences.en: And this was extremely dangerous, particularly in Poland.
sentences.zh: 这极其危险，尤其是在波兰。

sentences.en: The rescuers were just sent to the camps or even killed right away.
sentences.zh: 营救者会被直接送往集中营，甚至当场被杀。

sentences.en: So it was a very dangerous act.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种非常危险的行为。

sentences.en: So what did we think?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是怎么想的呢？

sentences.en: We thought, as an overall description, that women tended to be overrepresented when there was a very deeply relational kind of act as giving your kidney to another person.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，从总体描述来看，当涉及到像给他人捐肾这种深度关系导向的行为时，女性往往占比更高。

sentences.en: That's very deeply relational.
sentences.zh: 那是非常深度的关系导向。

sentences.en: And the Holocaust rescuing often was, too, because, you know, it would be a co-worker or a knock on the door
sentences.zh: 大屠杀营救往往也是如此，因为，你知道，可能是同事，或者是敲门声，

sentences.en: and you had to let people into your house and hide, you know, in the Anne Frank case to hide them.
sentences.zh: 你必须让人进屋躲藏，就像安妮·弗兰克那个案例一样，要把他们藏起来。

sentences.en: So this was very deeply relational.
sentences.zh: 所以这具有非常深度的关系性。

sentences.en: And so the women were somewhat overrepresented when the helping was of this type.
sentences.zh: 因此，当救助属于这种类型时，女性的比例会高一些。

sentences.en: And men were more overrepresented when the act demanded, often physical strength, of course, and some sudden action of rescue in a dangerous situation and stranger rescue.
sentences.zh: 而当行为需要体力，当然，以及在危险情况下采取突发行动和营救陌生人时，男性的比例更高。

sentences.en: You know, the person that's out there drowning is often not in your family.
sentences.zh: 你知道，溺水的人往往不是你的家人。

sentences.en: But, you know, you're at the beach and it becomes apparent.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你在海滩上，情况变得显而易见。

sentences.en: So that kind of stranger rescuing, demanding the very sudden decision, and often there was a, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以那种营救陌生人的行为，需要非常迅速的决定，而且通常，你知道，

sentences.en: could be a physical element in strength being an advantage that men are overrepresented.
sentences.zh: 可能存在体力优势的因素，这使得男性占比更高。

sentences.en: So there was some gendering in all of this.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切中确实存在某种性别差异。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这说得通。

sentences.en: I mean, especially if, I mean, a woman may say, oh, I'd like to run into that burning building and save those children.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特别是，如果一个女性可能会说，哦，我想冲进那栋着火的建筑去救那些孩子。

sentences.en: But I don't think I can, I could physically do that.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为我能做到，我体力上做不到。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're not sure you could, or it could be a man or a grown person in there.
sentences.zh: 是的，你不确定自己能否做到，或者里面可能是一个成年男性或成年人。

sentences.en: And you couldn't, and they are trained, of course, but firefighters.
sentences.zh: 你做不到，当然，消防员是受过训练的。

sentences.en: But ordinary people sometimes do those things, too, you know, not just the firefighter.
sentences.zh: 但普通人有时也会做这些事，你知道，不仅仅是消防员。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Well, let's step back for a minute and look at the big picture, because you've spent your career looking at differences and similarities between men and women.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们退后一步，从大局来看，因为你的职业生涯一直在观察男性和女性之间的差异与相似之处。

sentences.en: And during those years, there have been a lot of cultural changes.
sentences.zh: 在这些年里，发生了很多文化变革。

sentences.en: There are more women in the workforce today.
sentences.zh: 今天职场中有更多的女性。

sentences.en: Men are beginning to question the societal expectations for them to be tough and aggressive.
sentences.zh: 男性开始质疑社会对他们强硬和好斗的期望。

sentences.en: The Me Too movement has rendered some behaviors unacceptable.
sentences.zh: “我也是”（Me Too）运动使一些行为变得不可接受。

sentences.en: Are men and women, do you think, changing intrinsically through these upheavals?
sentences.zh: 你认为男性和女性是否正在经历这些剧变而发生本质上的改变？

sentences.en: Are the differences narrowing between what American society considers masculine and what it considers feminine?
sentences.zh: 美国社会所认为的男性气质和女性气质之间的差异是否正在缩小？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That is a very big question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常宏大的问题。

sentences.en: Certainly, women have changed profoundly by, you know, most women moving into the labor force, into a whole range of roles.
sentences.zh: 当然，女性已经发生了深刻的变化，你知道，大多数女性进入了劳动力市场，进入了各种各样的角色。

sentences.en: So women have had to, their lives have changed.
sentences.zh: 所以女性不得不改变，她们的生活已经改变了。

sentences.en: But if you look at that labor force, it's pretty segregated.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看劳动力市场，它还是相当隔离的。

sentences.en: So women tend to be in roles that are communally demanding, nursing and teaching and social work.
sentences.zh: 女性倾向于从事那些对共情要求较高的角色，如护理、教学和社会工作。

sentences.en: All women are overrepresented.
sentences.zh: 所有这些领域女性占比都过高。

sentences.en: You could say, well, yeah, but what about those other roles they've gone into?
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，好吧，是的，但她们进入的其他角色呢？

sentences.en: Like their lawyers and doctors, too, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 比如她们也成了律师和医生，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But then there's an internal segregation.
sentences.zh: 但内部依然存在隔离。

sentences.en: So look at public interest law.
sentences.zh: 看看公益法律领域。

sentences.en: You'll see a whole lot of women and family law, a whole lot of women.
sentences.zh: 你会看到大量的女性，还有家庭法领域，也有大量的女性。

sentences.en: And you look at medicine.
sentences.zh: 再看看医学领域。

sentences.en: It's obvious which specialty is most female dominated.
sentences.zh: 很明显哪个专业女性比例最高。

sentences.en: Pediatrics.
sentences.zh: 儿科。

sentences.en: Pediatrics.
sentences.zh: 儿科。

sentences.en: And, of course, gynecology and psychiatry, there are a lot of women.
sentences.zh: 当然，妇科和精神科也有很多女性。

sentences.en: So, again, in the more communally demanding areas and in management, in business, you could also guess which areas most female dominated.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，在更需要共情的领域，以及管理和商业领域，你也能猜到哪个领域女性比例最高。

sentences.en: Human resources.
sentences.zh: 人力资源。

sentences.en: And public relations, which demands, you know, a lot of social skill to go out there and represent your country.
sentences.zh: 还有公共关系，这需要，你知道，大量的社交技巧去走出去代表你的国家。

sentences.en: So there's, at some deep level of communion and agency, there's less change than people perhaps think because of the segregation not only between occupations,
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种深层的共情与能动性层面上，变化比人们想象的要少，因为不仅职业之间存在隔离，

sentences.en: but within occupations, at the kinds of subspecialties the women versus the men take on.
sentences.zh: 职业内部也存在隔离，即女性与男性所承担的亚专业类型不同。

sentences.en: So, yes, there's been enormous change.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，确实发生了巨大的变化。

sentences.en: You know, and we see in the stereotypes what's certainly ought to be there, which is the rise of women's communion.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在刻板印象中看到了肯定会出现的东西，那就是女性共情能力的提升。

sentences.en: Because, after all, women are more educated now, you know, than men, many more college degrees, and even the Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 因为毕竟，女性现在受教育程度更高了，你知道，比男性更高，拥有更多的大学学位，甚至博士学位

sentences.en: goes slightly in the female direction now.
sentences.zh: 现在也略微向女性倾斜。

sentences.en: So there's an enormous change in that kind of education, therefore, which produces knowledge and competence of that type.
sentences.zh: 所以这种教育发生了巨大的变化，从而产生了那种类型的知识和能力。

sentences.en: And so that's an enormous change of women becoming like men in that sense, but overtaking them.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的变化，女性在某种意义上变得像男性，甚至超越了他们。

sentences.en: So that's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: But there's this underlying agency of communion, the yin and yang dynamic, that we still see in the data.
sentences.zh: 但这种潜在的能动性与共情的阴阳动态，我们在数据中依然能看到。

sentences.en: And so we don't know what exactly that comes from.
sentences.zh: 所以我们并不确切知道这究竟源于什么。

sentences.en: You know, there's the nature-nurture question there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里涉及先天与后天的争论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So do you have any words of wisdom for those American women who are hoping someday to be president or CEO of a Fortune 500 company?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那些希望有朝一日成为美国总统或财富500强公司首席执行官的女性，您有什么建议吗？

sentences.en: What can they do in our current culture to improve their odds of success?
sentences.zh: 在当前的文化环境下，她们能做些什么来提高成功的几率？

sentences.en: Well, one thing we see, particularly in politics, in running for office,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们观察到的一点是，特别是在政治领域，在竞选公职时，

sentences.en: the women are more qualified in the sense they have more past experience in education that's relevant to the job.
sentences.zh: 女性的资质往往更高，因为她们在与工作相关的教育背景方面拥有更丰富的经验。

sentences.en: They're kind of overqualified in terms of those kinds of criteria.
sentences.zh: 从这些标准来看，她们甚至有点“超额”合格了。

sentences.en: I'm not sure the extent to which that's true in business, but I wouldn't be surprised.
sentences.zh: 我不确定在商业领域是否也是如此，但我对此并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So the idea would be don't skip on the qualifications.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的建议是不要在资质上打折扣。

sentences.en: You know, if most of those people have MBAs, get one and get one from the best place you can get one from.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果大多数人都有MBA学位，那你也要拿一个，而且要尽可能从最好的学校获得。

sentences.en: And then if you want to go into politics, OK, when you're young, you've got to get started.
sentences.zh: 如果你想投身政界，好吧，当你年轻时，就必须尽早开始。

sentences.en: When you're in college, go to the Republican or Democratic society for the students and try to get into leadership roles and then volunteer for campaigns.
sentences.zh: 在大学期间，加入共和党或民主党的学生社团，尝试担任领导职务，并为竞选活动做志愿者。

sentences.en: You know, get the knowledge, get the contacts, because they're probably going to be more important in general for the woman than the man.
sentences.zh: 去获取知识，建立人脉，因为对于女性来说，这些通常比男性更重要。

sentences.en: You know, we find that in politics, it's harder for women to get the, you know, the support and money for the campaign than it is for men.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在政治领域，女性比男性更难获得竞选所需的支持和资金。

sentences.en: So you've got to get well networked to compete.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须建立良好的人脉网络才能参与竞争。

sentences.en: So it's the route may be a little harder.
sentences.zh: 因此，这条路可能会稍微艰难一些。

sentences.en: Therefore, you have to have you have to bring more to bear.
sentences.zh: 所以，你必须付出更多的努力。

sentences.en: So don't skimp on it.
sentences.zh: 千万不要在这方面吝啬投入。

sentences.en: Don't think you could skimp on it.
sentences.zh: 别以为你可以省事。

sentences.en: So to get in there and get the kind of background that's as ideal as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以要深入其中，尽可能打下最理想的基础。

sentences.en: So that's very important.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: And then you do need to keep in mind the double bind.
sentences.zh: 此外，你还需要牢记“双重束缚”。

sentences.en: This is what we talked about before.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们之前讨论过的内容。

sentences.en: But another name is the double bind that as a woman, you're expected to be communal, to be kind and caring and, you know, nice.
sentences.zh: 另一个说法是“双重束缚”，即作为女性，社会期望你具有亲和力，要善良、体贴，你知道，要讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: And as a man, you're as a as a leader, rather, you're expected to be able to take charge and to be assertive and, you know, to be able to argue with people and hold your own.
sentences.zh: 而作为男性，或者说作为领导者，社会期望你能够掌控全局、果断自信，并且能够与人争论并坚持自己的立场。

sentences.en: So there's both of those things.
sentences.zh: 所以这两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: The man can just do the latter, you know, but the woman have to to be successful.
sentences.zh: 男性往往只需要做到后者，但女性要想成功，

sentences.en: People ordinarily have to bring the communion along because it's very important for them to be liked.
sentences.zh: 通常必须同时展现出亲和力，因为被人喜欢对她们来说非常重要。

sentences.en: Men can get away often with not being so liked.
sentences.zh: 男性往往即使不那么讨人喜欢也能过得去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the woman, if she's disliked, it's, you know, I think that was part of Hillary Clinton's problem.
sentences.zh: 但如果女性不被喜欢，你知道，我认为这就是希拉里·克林顿面临的问题之一。

sentences.en: A lot of people disliked Trump, but a lot of people disliked Hillary.
sentences.zh: 很多人不喜欢特朗普，但也有很多人不喜欢希拉里。

sentences.en: And I think that was a worse that was more of a disadvantage for her because she's a woman.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对她来说是一个更严重的劣势，因为她是女性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, to keep in mind the double bind and that you will have to negotiate it.
sentences.zh: 所以，要记住“双重束缚”，并且你必须学会应对它。

sentences.en: And there's smart ways to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且有聪明的应对方法。

sentences.en: I think Kamala Harris, insofar as I've seen her on television, is doing a good job with that.
sentences.zh: 我认为卡玛拉·哈里斯，就我在电视上看到的而言，在这方面做得很好。

sentences.en: You know, so look at women who appear to be doing a good job as role models.
sentences.zh: 所以，把那些看起来做得很好的女性当作榜样吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then persistence.
sentences.zh: 还有就是坚持不懈。

sentences.en: You know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的。

sentences.en: Because you're in that labyrinth.
sentences.zh: 因为你身处那个迷宫之中。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're in that.
sentences.zh: 是的，你就在其中。

sentences.en: Take a wrong turn.
sentences.zh: 走错了路，

sentences.en: Don't give up.
sentences.zh: 不要放弃。

sentences.en: Yeah, don't give up.
sentences.zh: 是的，不要放弃。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just learn from it.
sentences.zh: 从中吸取教训就好。

sentences.en: You know, when things go bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当事情进展不顺时。

sentences.en: In all careers, many things I've done, I wish had gone better or I did something wrong.
sentences.zh: 在所有的职业生涯中，我做过很多事，有些我希望当时能做得更好，或者我确实做错了什么。

sentences.en: But, you know, I hung in there.
sentences.zh: 但是，我坚持了下来。

sentences.en: So, that's important in all careers.
sentences.zh: 所以，这在所有职业中都很重要。

sentences.en: But if you're in a career that has a labyrinth, then it's even more important.
sentences.zh: 但如果你从事的是一个充满“迷宫”的职业，那就更加重要了。

sentences.en: You know, you could get discouraged, but take a deep breath and learn from it and go on.
sentences.zh: 你可能会感到气馁，但深呼吸，从中学习，然后继续前进。

sentences.en: And, yeah, so I think, you know, I admire women who do make it through to these leadership roles.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我很钦佩那些最终走上领导岗位的女性。

sentences.en: Because I think on the average, it just takes more skill than it did for the man in leadership.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为平均而言，这比男性担任领导职务需要更多的技能。

sentences.en: You know, he wouldn't be so much tested and questioned as to whether he could do the job.
sentences.zh: 男性不会受到那么多的考验和质疑，不会被问及是否能胜任这份工作。

sentences.en: Sounds a little unfair, but I guess you just have to put up with that, right?
sentences.zh: 听起来有点不公平，但我想你只能忍受这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: It's unfair, but it's like you also have a burden for the people who become – the women become – come along later, you know.
sentences.zh: 这确实不公平，但这也意味着你肩负着为后来者——那些随后出现的女性——铺路的责任。

sentences.en: So, we could be thankful for Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们应该感谢希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That she was there and got people used to it.
sentences.zh: 因为她身处其中，让人们习惯了女性担任这些角色。

sentences.en: No, she didn't win, but she won the popular vote.
sentences.zh: 不，她没有赢，但她赢得了普选票。

sentences.en: Hey, come on now.
sentences.zh: 嘿，别这样。

sentences.en: So, the women that come next, like Kamala Harris, I think have an easier time because of her and other women in politics.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为像卡玛拉·哈里斯这样的后来者，因为她和其他女性在政界的努力，会走得更容易一些。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so we have to think it's unfair, but it's not as unfair as it was earlier because they were there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们必须承认这不公平，但比起过去，已经没那么不公平了，因为她们曾经努力过。

sentences.en: And I hope to make it less unfair for the women who come next.
sentences.zh: 我也希望能为后来者减少这种不公平。

sentences.en: That's a good way to look at it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的看待方式。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Egley, thank you so much for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，埃格利博士，非常感谢您今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting and just a very – almost a fun conversation to have.
sentences.zh: 这次谈话非常有趣，甚至可以说是一次愉快的交流。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: I enjoyed talking with you.
sentences.zh: 我很享受与你的交谈。

sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org 或您获取播客的任何平台找到《心理学谈话》的往期节目。

sentences.zh: 如果您有任何评论或对未来节目的想法，请发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 地址是 speakingofpsychology，连在一起，@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频编辑是克里斯·康达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯，代表美国心理学会。
